page: Microsoft Azure E4bds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture and orchestrated by Microsoft Hyper-V. It provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB to 1 vCPU allocation ratio. This elevated memory density targets workloads whose working sets exceed conventional general-purpose specifications, preventing memory paging under sustained operational loads.

Storage configuration includes an integrated 236 GB local NVMe solid-state disk designed for low-latency temporary data, scratch space, and swap files. Additionally, the instance supports high-performance remote block storage integration for persistent workloads. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its execution strictly toward CPU and memory operations. The instance provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network gateways or managed routing configurations for external ingress and egress connectivity.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency standpoint, the instance minimizes compute overhead for applications constrained primarily by memory rather than processing capacity. Deploying memory-bound services on this specification avoids over-provisioning CPU cores simply to satisfy RAM requirements. The presence of local NVMe storage reduces external input and output calls for transient data, controlling remote disk transactions. Azure E4bds_v6 is technically suited for medium-scale relational databases, in-memory caches, distributed processing nodes, search indexing services, and enterprise analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E4bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processor cores managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 4 vCPUs paired with 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per core ratio that caters to memory-intensive software footprints. Storage capabilities include an integrated 236 GB local NVMe SSD alongside premium block storage connectivity, allowing low-latency local caching and durable external volume attachments. The configuration contains no dedicated hardware graphics accelerators and excludes complimentary public IPv4 addressing. By allocating substantial memory density relative to compute resources, the instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for architectures where memory capacity dictates instance sizing rather than raw execution throughput. The platform presents a balanced profile for transactional databases, in-memory caching nodes, search indices, batch analytics, and data pipeline tasks that require fast local scratch disks combined with a reliable memory subsystem.
